Create a 90-day action plan for my business. Here's my current situation:
- Business: [describe what you do]
- Revenue: [current monthly revenue]
- Biggest bottleneck: [what's holding you back]
- Goal for the next 90 days: [your #1 goal — e.g., "get to $20K/month" or "launch my course" or "hire my first employee"]
- Resources: [budget, time per week, team size]
Give me: (1) The 3 highest-leverage things I should focus on (and what I should STOP doing), (2) A month-by-month breakdown with specific milestones, (3) Weekly priorities for Month 1 (the most detailed), (4) Key metrics I should track to know if I'm on pace, (5) Risks and contingency plans, (6) The one thing that will matter most. Be brutally honest about what actually moves the needle vs. what feels productive but isn't.

Create a one-page annual strategic plan for my business for [year].
Context:
- Business: [describe]
- Last year's revenue: [amount]
- Last year's biggest win: [describe]
- Last year's biggest lesson: [describe]
- Revenue goal for this year: [target]
- Key assumption: [what needs to be true for the plan to work]
One-page plan should include: (1) Vision statement (where I want to be Dec 31), (2) 3 Strategic Priorities for the year, (3) For each priority: 2-3 measurable targets, (4) Quarterly milestones (what "on track" looks like at Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4), (5) Resources needed (budget, hires, tools), (6) What I'm saying NO to this year (just as important), (7) My "North Star Metric" — the single number that matters most. Make it fit on one page. This goes on my wall.

I need to make a decision about [describe your decision — e.g., "whether to hire a full-time employee vs. keep using contractors" or "whether to launch a new product line" or "whether to take on a large client that would consume 60% of my capacity"].
Here's the context:
- Option A: [describe]
- Option B: [describe]
- Option C (if applicable): [describe]
- My constraints: [time, money, risk tolerance, goals]
- What I'm afraid of: [be honest — what's the worst case?]
Walk me through a structured decision analysis: (1) Pros and cons of each option (weighted by importance), (2) Second-order consequences (what happens 6-12 months after each choice), (3) The "regret minimization" test — which choice would I most regret NOT making? (4) A "reversibility" check — which decisions are easy to undo vs. hard to undo? (5) Your recommendation and reasoning. Be direct. Don't hedge.

Help me set OKRs (Objectives and Key Results) for next quarter. My business is [describe]. Current state: [revenue, team size, stage].
My top priorities are:
1. [Priority 1 — e.g., "grow revenue"]
2. [Priority 2 — e.g., "build repeatable lead generation"]
3. [Priority 3 — e.g., "improve client retention"]
For each priority, give me: (1) An Objective (ambitious but achievable, qualitative, inspiring), (2) 3 Key Results (specific, measurable, time-bound — numbers I can actually track), (3) 2-3 Initiatives (the actual projects/tasks that will drive the key results). Also: flag which OKR is the most important (if I can only focus on one), and suggest a simple weekly check-in format to track progress. Keep it realistic for a [solo / small team] — not a Google-sized OKR system.

Create a quarterly business review (QBR) template I can fill out every 90 days to track my business health. Structure:
1. Scorecard: Key metrics dashboard — revenue, profit margin, client count, lead count, [2-3 metrics specific to my business type: [describe]], and comparison to last quarter
2. What Worked: Top 3 wins and why they happened (so I can repeat them)
3. What Didn't Work: Top 3 misses and what I learned (so I don't repeat them)
4. Goal Review: Last quarter's goals — hit/miss with brief explanation for each
5. Client/Customer Review: Who came, who left, NPS or satisfaction trends
6. Financial Review: Revenue trend, expense trend, cash position
7. Team/Resource Review: Who/what I need that I don't have
8. Next Quarter Goals: 3 goals with measurable targets
9. Top Priorities: The 1-3 projects or initiatives that will drive those goals
10. Risks & Contingencies: What could derail the plan and my backup
Include guiding questions under each section to make it easy to fill out. This should take 1-2 hours max.

My business currently makes money from [describe your revenue streams and what % each represents — e.g., "80% client services, 20% digital products"]. I'm worried about [your concern — e.g., "being too dependent on one income source" or "revenue being tied to my time"].
Help me build a revenue diversification plan: (1) Assess my current risk — how concentrated is my revenue and why that's a problem, (2) Identify 3-5 adjacent revenue streams I could add based on my skills and audience (for context: my audience is [describe] and I'm known for [expertise]), (3) For each new stream: estimated revenue potential, time to launch, effort to maintain, and how it complements my existing business, (4) A recommended implementation order (what to add first), (5) What each revenue mix could look like in 12 months. Be realistic about a solopreneur's capacity.

Create an end-of-year financial review document template for my [type of business]. Structure it as:
1. Year in Numbers: Total revenue, total expenses, net profit, YoY growth (with comparison placeholders)
2. Revenue Breakdown: By service/product line, by client, by month (suggest a table format)
3. Expense Breakdown: By category, highlight what increased/decreased and why
4. Key Wins: Biggest revenue months, largest deals, new revenue streams
5. Key Lessons: What cost more than expected, what I'd cut, what I'd invest more in
6. Client Analysis: Top clients by revenue, client retention rate, average project value
7. Goals vs. Actuals: Compare what I planned for the year vs. what happened
8. Next Year Plan: Revenue target, expense budget, key investments, risks to watch
Include prompts/questions under each section to help me fill it out. This should make me feel like I have a CFO.
